## Load R packages
```{r}
# Load required packages for multi-omics analysis
# mixOmics: provides tools for multivariate analysis and integration of omics datasets
# Reference: http://mixomics.org/
library(mixOmics)

# tidyverse: collection of R packages for data manipulation and visualization
library(tidyverse)

# Set seed for reproducibility - ensures that random processes (like cross-validation)
# produce the same results each time the code is run
set.seed(123)
```


## Import all omics
```{r}
# Import multi-omics data for Streptococcus pyogenes
# Each dataset contains measurements across different molecular layers:

# 1. Transcriptomics data: gene expression levels (RNA-seq)
# Rows = samples, Columns = genes/transcripts
Strep_trans_data <- read.csv("/Users/wmujchariyak/Desktop/Strep_transcriptome_data.csv", header = TRUE) %>% 
  column_to_rownames(var = "X")  # Move first column (sample IDs) to row names

# 2. Proteomics data: protein abundance levels (mass spectrometry)
# Rows = samples, Columns = proteins
Strep_prot_data <- read.csv("/Users/wmujchariyak/Desktop/Strep_proteome_data.csv", header = TRUE) %>% 
  column_to_rownames(var = "X")

# 3. Metabolomics data: metabolite concentrations (GC-MS)
# Rows = samples, Columns = metabolites
Strep_met_GC_data <- read.csv("/Users/wmujchariyak/Desktop/Strep_metabolome_GC_data.csv", header = TRUE) %>% 
  column_to_rownames(var = "X")
```


## Data for MixOmics 
```{r}
# Organize data into a named list structure required by mixOmics
# This format allows for easy iteration over multiple omics datasets
data <- list(Transcript = Strep_trans_data, 
             Protein = Strep_prot_data, 
             Metabolite_GC = Strep_met_GC_data)

# Check dimensions of each dataset (should have same number of rows = samples)
# Expected output: number of samples (rows) x number of features (columns) for each omics layer
lapply(data, dim)

# Create response variable (Y) representing experimental conditions
# RPMI: standard bacterial culture medium (control condition)
# SERUM: medium supplemented with serum (experimental condition)
# Each condition has 30 biological replicates (60 total samples)
Y <- factor(rep(c("RPMI", "SERUM"), 30))

# Verify the distribution of samples across conditions
summary(Y)
```

## PCA 
```{r}
# Principal Component Analysis (PCA) - Unsupervised dimensionality reduction
# PCA is used to explore the overall structure of each omics dataset independently
# Reference: http://mixomics.org/methods/pca/
# Tutorial: http://mixomics.org/case-studies/pca-liver-toxicity/

# Initialize storage lists for results from each omics layer
data_name <- c("Transcript", "Protein", "Metabolite_GC")
list.final.pca <- list()      # Store final PCA models
plot.tune.pca <- list()        # Store tuning results
pca.cum.var <- list()          # Store cumulative variance explained

# Perform PCA for each omics dataset
for (i in seq_along(data_name)){
  set.seed(123)  # Ensure reproducibility within the loop
  data_pca <- data[[i]]
  
  # Step 1: Tune the number of principal components
  # tune.pca() evaluates how much variance is explained by each component
  # ncomp = 10: test up to 10 principal components
  # scale = TRUE: standardize variables (mean=0, variance=1) to ensure comparability
  # This is crucial when features are measured in different units
  tune.pca <- tune.pca(data_pca, ncomp = 10, scale = TRUE)
  plot.tune.pca[[i]] <- tune.pca
  
  # Extract cumulative proportion of variance explained
  # Helps determine optimal number of components to retain
  pca.cum.var[[i]] <- tune.pca$cum.var       
  
  # Step 2: Perform final PCA with chosen number of components
  # ncomp = 3: retain first 3 principal components (based on tuning results)
  # These 3 components typically capture ~50% of the total variance
  final.pca <- pca(data_pca, ncomp = 3, scale = TRUE)
  list.final.pca[[i]] <- final.pca
}

# Note: Results from "tune.pca" suggest that using 3 components can cover almost 50% 
# of variation in the datasets, providing a good balance between data reduction and 
# information retention
```

## Data visualization - Preliminary
```{r}
# Explore variable contributions (loadings) for each omics layer
# Loadings indicate which features contribute most to each principal component
# Reference: http://mixomics.org/graphics/sample-plots/plotloadings/

# Transcriptomics loadings
# plotLoadings shows the most important genes contributing to PC1
# comp = 1: visualize loadings for the first principal component
# method = 'mean': order features by their mean absolute loading value
# contrib = 'max': keep only features with maximum contribution
plotLoadings(list.final.pca[[1]], comp = 1, method = 'mean', contrib = 'max', size.title = rel(1))

# Extract and rank transcript variables by their contribution to PC1
trans.pca.var <- selectVar(list.final.pca[[1]], comp = 1)$value
trans.pca.var$Rank <- rank(abs(trans.pca.var$value.var))

# Proteomics loadings
# Identify key proteins driving variation along PC1
plotLoadings(list.final.pca[[2]], comp = 1, method = 'mean', contrib = 'max', size.title = rel(1))

# Extract and rank protein variables
prot.ms1.pca.var <- selectVar(list.final.pca[[2]], comp = 1)$value
prot.ms1.pca.var$Rank <- rank(abs(prot.ms1.pca.var$value.var))

# Metabolomics loadings (GC-MS)
# Identify key metabolites contributing to separation between conditions
plotLoadings(list.final.pca[[3]], comp = 1, method = 'mean', contrib = 'max', size.title = rel(1))

# Extract and rank metabolite variables
met.LC.pca.var <- selectVar(list.final.pca[[3]], comp = 1)$value
met.LC.pca.var$Rank <- rank(abs(met.LC.pca.var$value.var))
```

## Data visualization - Final 
```{r}
# Create sample plots (score plots) to visualize sample clustering in PCA space
# These plots show how samples separate based on their molecular profiles
# Reference: http://mixomics.org/graphics/sample-plots/plotindiv/

# Transcriptome PCA plot
# Visualizes samples projected onto the first two principal components
# Each point represents one sample, colored by experimental condition
plotIndiv_pca_trans <- plotIndiv(list.final.pca[[1]], 
                                  group = Y,              # Color samples by condition (RPMI vs SERUM)
                                  ind.names = FALSE,      # Don't show individual sample names (cleaner plot)
                                  legend = TRUE,          # Display legend for groups
                                  ellipse = TRUE,         # Draw confidence ellipses around groups
                                  style = "ggplot2",      # Use ggplot2-style graphics
                                  size.title = rel(2.5),  # Enlarge title
                                  size.xlabel = rel(1.5), # Enlarge x-axis label
                                  size.ylabel = rel(1.5), # Enlarge y-axis label
                                  title = 'Transcriptome')

# Proteome PCA plot
# Shows protein-level separation between conditions
plotIndiv_pca_prot <- plotIndiv(list.final.pca[[2]], 
                                 group = Y, 
                                 ind.names = FALSE,
                                 legend = TRUE, 
                                 ellipse = TRUE, 
                                 style = "ggplot2", 
                                 size.title = rel(2.5),
                                 size.xlabel = rel(1.5), 
                                 size.ylabel = rel(1.5),
                                 title = 'Proteome')

# Metabolome PCA plot (GC-MS)
# Reveals metabolite-level differences between growth conditions
plotIndiv_pca_met_GC <- plotIndiv(list.final.pca[[3]], 
                                   group = Y, 
                                   ind.names = FALSE,
                                   legend = TRUE, 
                                   ellipse = TRUE, 
                                   style = "ggplot2", 
                                   size.title = rel(2.5),
                                   size.xlabel = rel(1.5), 
                                   size.ylabel = rel(1.5),
                                   title = 'Metabolome (GC-MS)')

# Interpretation:
# - Distinct clusters indicate that conditions have different molecular signatures
# - Ellipse overlap suggests similarity between conditions at that omics level
# - Distance between samples reflects their molecular dissimilarity
```
